item.title: Ebola: Lagos Intensifies Surveillance, Reassures Residents Of Preparedness

item.title: ‘Filled with content creators’ — Bwala disparages NDC campaign council list
item.description: Daniel Bwala, an aide to President Bola Tinubu, has criticised the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) over its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections, describing the list as being “filled with content creators”. Bwala, in a post on X shortly after the party announced the council on Sunday, also accused the NDC of concealing the identities of its media surrogates in mainstream media. “@PeterObi and NDC have released their list of campaign council members; and as expected it is filled with content creators,” he wrote. “They stylishly refused to name their campaign media surrogates in the mainstream media masquerading as OAP.” @PeterObi and NDC have released their list of campaign council members; and as expected it is filled with content creators. They stylishly refused to name their campaign media surrogates in the mainstream media masquerading as OAP. — D. H Bwala (@BwalaDaniel) October 25, 2026 The NDC had earlier announced the constitution of its National Campaign Council, saying it would coordinate campaign activities nationwide and mobilise support for its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Under the arrangement, the party’s National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, will serve as chairman, while its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will be co-chairman. The party’s National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, was named vice-chairman, while its vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, will serve as co-vice-chairman. The NDC’s National Secretary, Barrister Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, was named council secretary, while Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim will serve as director-general. Announcing the council, the party said it would provide “strategic leadership” and drive nationwide mobilisation behind its vision of “a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria”. The NDC also said the council would deliver a “people-centred and issue-based campaign” and urged its members, supporters and other Nigerians to remain united ahead of the elections. Bwala’s comments came shortly after the announcement, as political parties prepare their structures and mobilisation strategies for the 2027 general elections. item.title: 2027: NDC releases campaign council list, names Dickson chairman, Obi co-chair
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has named its National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, as chairman of its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections, with its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as co-chairman. The party announced the constitution of the council in a statement posted on its X account on Sunday. The council is expected to coordinate the party’s campaign activities nationwide and mobilise support for its candidates ahead of the elections. According to the announcement, NDC National Chairman Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe will serve as vice-chairman, while the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has been named co-vice-chairman. The party’s National Secretary, Barrister Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, will serve as council secretary, while Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim has been appointed director-general. Announcing the appointments, the NDC said the council would provide strategic leadership for its campaign and coordinate mobilisation efforts across the country. “The National Campaign Council will provide strategic leadership, coordinate campaign activities across the country, and drive the mobilisation of Nigerians behind the party’s vision of a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria,” the statement said. The party said the council would work towards delivering a campaign focused on the needs of Nigerians and policy issues. It described its proposed campaign as “people-centred and issue-based”, while urging party members and supporters to remain united ahead of the 2027 elections. “We call on all party members, supporters, and well-meaning Nigerians to remain united and focused as we work together to rescue our country,” the NDC said. The announcement comes as political parties begin preparations for the 2027 general elections, with campaigns expected to focus on candidates, policy proposals and nationwide mobilisation. item.title: Opebi-Mende-Ojota Link Bridge To Be Opened Before Christmas, Says Sanwo-Olu
item.description: The Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has said that the Opebi-Mende Link Bridge is about 80 per cent complete, expressing confidence that the project will be opened to the public before Christmas. Governor Sanwo-Olu gave the assurance during an inspection of the project, acknowledging that the construction had exceeded the September completion timeline previously announced. He said his visit to the site was to establish the reasons for the delay and assess the progress of work, stressing that the project’s distinctive architectural design and engineering requirements must not be compromised by the pressure to meet the deadline. He explained that the bridge’s steel structure was designed to reflect the area’s historical association with cane weaving, thereby preserving its cultural identity. According to him, the project involves installing more than 300 tonnes of steel at heights of up to 25 metres, making it an unusually demanding engineering undertaking. The governor said three of the four major steel components, designed to resemble interwoven cane, had been completed, while work was ongoing on the remaining component. He added that light-emitting diode (LED) installations featuring the colours of Lagos State would enhance the structure and give it an iconic appearance. Governor Sanwo-Olu added that the state government would not sacrifice engineering quality and public safety for speed, despite the delay. He said additional activities, including site cleaning, repainting of kerbs, restoration of affected areas and landscaping, would be undertaken before the bridge is opened to the public. He envisaged the area becoming a destination for recreation, cultural heritage and tourism, adding that its redevelopment would enable residents to appreciate the history and identity of the community. The governor maintained that the bridge would become a significant infrastructure landmark in Lagos, combining innovation with cultural preservation. Sanwo-Olu commissioned the construction of the bridge in 2022 to ease congestion in Ikeja and environs. Governor Sanwo-Olu (centre) He said that the bridge, which is part of the ‘legacy project,’ was an innovative solution to the perennial gridlock around Opebi/Mobolaji Bank Anthony Way/Ojota/Mende corridor. item.title: Bayern beat Freiburg to reclaim top spot as Kompany remains hospitalised
item.description: Bayern Munich reclaimed top spot in the Bundesliga with a 3-1 win at Freiburg on Sunday, days after coach Vincent Kompany was hospitalised when he collapsed at training. Bayern were missing several first-team players and Kompany, but cruised to a two-goal lead at half-time with Dayot Upamecano and Serge Gnabry scoring. Freiburg pulled one back and were pushing for a point in stoppage time when goalkeeper Mio Backhaus was caught out up the field, allowing Michael Olise to slide the ball into an empty net. Kompany remains in hospital and is being treated for a mystery virus, with Bayern saying Saturday the coach is likely to be out for “days, not weeks”. “I just opened my phone to a message from Vince saying ‘well done’ and he was happy,” assistant coach Aaron Danks told DAZN. “I just replied saying ‘brilliant — now go rest’. I sent him a kissing emoji, so hopefully he rests up.” Bayern sporting director Max Eberl gave an update on Kompany’s condition. “He’s stable. He no longer has a headache. He’s now undergoing a thorough examination. Everything is being handled,” he said. “There’s no diagnosis, nothing final yet.” With victory Bayern leapfrogged Borussia Dortmund to top the table ahead of the duo’s clash in Munich next week. Harry Kane had a close-range effort saved late in the second half but failed to find the net a day before the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, with the England captain among the favourites. Bayern arrived in the Black Forest after a tumultuous few days which left them lacking leaders. With coach Kompany still in hospital after collapsing on Friday, Englishman Danks was in the dugout. The visitors were also without injured captain Manuel Neuer, Luis Diaz, Jamal Musiala, Aleksandar Pavlovic and Kim Min-jae, while midfielder and Germany captain Joshua Kimmich was on bereavement leave due to the sudden death of his father. Bayern were in the unusual position of sitting back and absorbing pressure as Freiburg pushed, but took the lead after 16 minutes when Upamecano started and finished a length-of-the-field counter. The France defender won possession near his own box, played a one-two with Olise before thundering goalwards and sending a cool shot past Backhaus. Bayern doubled up just before the break when Gnabry latched onto a Nathaniel Brown pass and nutmegged Backhaus to score. With 10 minutes remaining, Kane stung Backhaus’s palms from close range and the hosts went on an immediate counter, forcing Tom Bischof into conceding an own goal. The goal sparked Freiburg to life and Bayern ‘keeper Jonas Urbig needed to make crucial saves from Igor Matanovic in the dying moments. item.description: The recent voter registration figures released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) have raised important questions about the declining number of young people on Nigeria’s voter register. The 2026 age distribution is as follows: • Youth: 18–34 years: 29,777,578 (28.79 per cent) • Middle age: 35–49 years: 43,265,946 (41.83 per cent) • Elderly: 50–69 years: 22,982,900 (22.22 per cent) • 70 years and above: 7,402,291 (7.16 per cent) What Do These Figures Tell Us? 1. item.title: 2027: Keyamo to lead APC presidential campaign air operations
item.description: By Dickson Omobola President Bola Tinubu has appointed Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, to head the Directorate of Air Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 re-election campaign Keyamo would serve as Director of the Directorate of Air Mobilisation, with the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, Mrs Olubunmi Kuku, appointed Deputy Director 1, while Engr Farouk Ahmed Umar would serve as Deputy Director II. Special Adviser on Media and Communications to the Minister, Tunde Moshood, in a statement, said the appointments underscored the strategic importance of air transportation, operational coordination and aviation logistics to the organisation of a nationwide presidential campaign in a country as geographically extensive as Nigeria. The statement reads: ‘The Directorate of Air Mobilisation is expected to play a crucial role in coordinating the campaign’s air-movement requirements, facilitating travel arrangements for designated campaign officials and personnel, and ensuring effective planning for air transportation in support of campaign activities across the six geopolitical zones of the country. “Given the scale of the 2027 presidential campaign, the directorate is expected to work closely with other relevant campaign structures to promote seamless coordination, operational efficiency and effective deployment of available logistical resources, subject to applicable aviation regulations and electoral laws. “Keyamo’s appointment brings to the campaign structure the experience of a serving aviation minister who has been at the forefront of policy initiatives aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s aviation sector, improving its international standing and positioning the country as a major aviation hub in Africa. “His familiarity with the operational demands of the aviation industry is expected to provide useful leadership in coordinating the directorate’s activities and establishing an effective framework for air-mobilisation planning. “The appointment of Mrs. Olubunmi Kuku and Umar as Deputy Directors also brings aviation-sector leadership and technical experience into the directorate, strengthening its capacity to address the planning and coordination demands associated with nationwide campaign movements.” The post 2027: Keyamo to lead APC presidential campaign air operations appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Learn leadership from Macron amid killings, hardship – ADC to Tinubu
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) on Sunday challenged President Bola Tinubu to learn from French President Emmanuel Macron, accusing him of failing to show sufficient empathy for Nigerians grappling with insecurity, hunger and economic hardship. The council said the reported postponement of Macron’s scheduled state visit to Nigeria underscored the need for leaders to pay attention to pressing domestic challenges, arguing that Nigerians facing killings, mass abductions and rising living costs deserve more visible concern from their president. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC cited reports that Macron had rescheduled his October 28–29, 2026 visit to Nigeria, including the planned France-Nigeria Business Forum in Lagos, to early 2027 amid domestic challenges in France. “A president will not travel when his home is contending with internal combustion,” a Nigerian official familiar with the development was quoted as saying. The ADC-PCC said the welfare of citizens should remain central to governance, citing attacks and killings in Plateau, Niger, Benue, Zamfara, Kaduna, Kogi, Kwara, Katsina, Sokoto and other parts of the country. It also raised concerns over a reported incident in Niger State involving the detention of more than 60 young Nigerians under allegedly inhumane conditions, with over 37 reportedly dying in custody. Describing the incident as a grave national concern, the council demanded urgent government intervention, accountability and justice for the affected families. It faulted Tinubu’s response, claiming that Vice President Kashim Shettima visited the state weeks after the incident, following a visit by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to commiserate with affected communities and bereaved families. The council said Atiku’s visit demonstrated the importance of identifying with citizens in moments of grief, arguing that public office holders must show concern through direct engagement with affected people, not merely official statements. “President Macron has offered a reminder that the concerns of citizens must remain central to leadership. When a country faces a serious domestic crisis, its leadership must demonstrate urgency, compassion and a willingness to take responsibility,” the council said. The ADC-PCC urged the Tinubu administration to prioritise the protection of lives, tackle insecurity and ease the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. It also demanded answers over deaths in custody and alleged unlawful detention, insisting that affected families deserved justice and those responsible should be held accountable. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC cited reports that Macron had rescheduled his October 28–29, 2026 visit to Nigeria, including the planned France-Nigeria Business Forum in Lagos, to early 2027 amid domestic challenges in France. “A president will not travel when his home is contending with internal combustion,” a Nigerian official familiar with the development was quoted as saying. The ADC-PCC said the welfare of citizens should remain central to governance, citing attacks and killings in Plateau, Niger, Benue, Zamfara, Kaduna, Kogi, Kwara, Katsina, Sokoto and other parts of the country. It also raised concerns over a reported incident in Niger State involving the detention of more than 60 young Nigerians under allegedly inhumane conditions, with over 37 reportedly dying in custody. Describing the incident as a grave national concern, the council demanded urgent government intervention, accountability and justice for the affected families. It faulted Tinubu’s response, claiming that Vice President Kashim Shettima visited the state weeks after the incident, following a visit by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to commiserate with affected communities and bereaved families. The council said Atiku’s visit demonstrated the importance of identifying with citizens in moments of grief, arguing that public office holders must show concern through direct engagement with affected people, not merely official statements. “President Macron has offered a reminder that the concerns of citizens must remain central to leadership. When a country faces a serious domestic crisis, its leadership must demonstrate urgency, compassion and a willingness to take responsibility,” the council said. The ADC-PCC urged the Tinubu administration to prioritise the protection of lives, tackle insecurity and ease the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. It also demanded answers over deaths in custody and alleged unlawful detention, insisting that affected families deserved justice and those responsible should be held accountable. item.title: 2027: PDP meets INEC deadline on omitted candidates

item.title: My father saw acting as prostitution — Uzoamaka Power
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Actress Uzoamaka Power, known for her role in The Call of My Life, has revealed that her father’s perception of acting initially made her afraid to pursue her dream of becoming an actress. Speaking during an interview on the Tea With Tay podcast, Power recalled how her father frequently criticised actresses whenever they appeared on television, questioning their dressing and commitment to education. “With my father, I was cowardly about pursuing my dreams because my father’s idea of acting, the way he saw acting, was prostitution,” she said. According to her, watching films with her father often meant listening to his disapproval of the women appearing on screen. “Anytime we watched a film, he was always criticising the women. He would be like, ‘Don’t they have parents? Look at what they are wearing, and they are in the university. When do they have time to study?’” Despite his reservations, Power said she had always been certain about her desire to become an actress and believed she would succeed in the profession. “I had a knowing in me that I was going to be an actor, and I knew I was going to succeed doing this thing I love doing,” she said. The actress, however, acknowledged that her father’s concerns came from a place of care, explaining that he wanted her to pursue a career he considered more financially secure. “I understood that he was looking out for me and he wanted the best for me. He also knew these kinds of jobs were not sustainable. You needed, like, an office job,” she recalled. Speaking further about her personality and how she handles perceptions of arrogance, Power maintained that she had never felt the need to diminish herself to make others comfortable. “I have never felt the need to downplay myself or to make myself feel small for the benefit of everyone else. I have always known who I am. I have always known my shortcomings, to be honest,” she said. She added that being aware of her strengths and limitations had helped her remain comfortable with herself, regardless of how others interpreted her confidence. “I am very honest with myself about where I am, what I am doing, what I am capable of, what I am unable to do, and whether I am willing to learn. “So, I have just been myself, really. And if anyone considers that not being humble, I am sorry, I can’t,” she said. The post My father saw acting as prostitution — Uzoamaka Power appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police Foil Railway Vandalism, Arrest Four Suspects With 70 Stolen Sleepers In Katsina
item.description: The Katsina State Police Command has arrested four suspected railway vandals and recovered 70 railway sleepers believed to have been stolen. The suspects were apprehended on October 11, 2026, at about 12:30 a.m., when police operatives on routine stop-and-search duty along the Kurfi–Tsanni Village Road intercepted a white J5 vehicle. The vehicle, driven by a 25-year-old man, was said to be carrying three other occupants. A thorough search of the vehicle uncovered 70 railway sleepers carefully concealed behind 17 bags of animal feed in what investigators believe was an attempt to evade detection. Police said preliminary investigations revealed that one of the suspects confessed to receiving the railway materials from a suspected supplier from Bauchi State, who is currently at large. The police said 70 railway sleepers were carefully concealed behind 17 bags of animal feed in what investigators believe was an attempt to evade detection. According to the police command, the stolen items were being transported for delivery to a man in Katsina. It said that the four suspects are currently in police custody, while the operational vehicle, the recovered railway sleepers and the bags of animal feed used to conceal them have been secured as exhibits. The Command said efforts are underway to apprehend the fleeing suspects and determine the exact location from which the railway infrastructure was vandalised, adding that investigations are ongoing. In a statement issued on Sunday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Abubakar Sadiq, described the arrests as another breakthrough in the fight against crimes targeting critical national infrastructure. Sadiq said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ali Umar Fage, reaffirmed the Command’s unwavering commitment to protecting critical national infrastructure and bringing perpetrators of vandalism to justice. The PPRO said that the commissioner also appealed to residents to continue supporting security agencies with timely and credible information that will enable the police to prevent crime and swiftly apprehend criminal elements across the state. item.title: Is Wizkid failing his fans in 2026?
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi It appears music powerhouse Ayodeji Balogun is keeping his fans hanging too long on a thread after he made a promise of his seventh solo studio album “coming soon” in June 2026. Three months down the line, the wait continues without any actual date in sight. The Wizkid FC, his fanatical fans, wouldn’t throw any tantrum about this, but the question has to be asked as to what is keeping the “Holla at Ya Boy” star from unleashing his “Sexy” (title of his seventh studio album) on the music scene. The fact that the superstar started 2026 on the up and up hasn’t helped matters because it felt pretty much like he gave his fans a shot in the arm and left them high and dry. He began the year with ‘Jogodo’, a collaboration with Asake that set the stage for their joint extended play, ‘REAL, Vol. 1’. He subsequently expanded his catalogue with releases involving Latin music, British R&B and other contemporary sounds, reinforcing his reputation as an artiste comfortable working across musical boundaries. One of the defining moments of his 2026 output was the January release of ‘REAL, Vol. 1’, a four-track EP with Asake. Released on January 23, the project brought together two generations of Nigerian music stars whose styles have helped shape the contemporary Afrobeats sound. The project followed the success of their earlier collaborations, including ‘MMS’ on Asake’s 2024 album, ‘Lungu Boy’. It featured songs such as ‘Jogodo’, ‘Iskolodo’ and ‘Turbulence’, combining infectious rhythms, melodic hooks and elements of contemporary African dance music. ‘Jogodo’, released ahead of the EP in January, served as the lead single and generated anticipation for the full project. The collaboration offered fans an opportunity to hear the two singers build on their established musical chemistry. The singer continued this international run with ‘Alive’, a collaboration with British singer-songwriter Jorja Smith, released on July 2. The song blended R&B and Afrobeats, with production by P2J, and appeared ahead of Smith’s third studio album, ‘What Are The Odds’. Another notable release was ‘Coca Body’, featuring Dutch rapper and singer Frenna, British-Nigerian singer Odeal and Wizkid. Released in July, the song brought together the artistes’ melodic approaches in a record that drew on Afrobeats, R&B and hip-hop influences. These collaborations highlighted Wizkid’s continued willingness to explore different sounds while maintaining the relaxed vocal delivery that has become a hallmark of his music. Beyond his recorded collaborative outputs, his fans still await his next solo effort. In June, he unveiled ‘Sexy’ as the title of his seventh studio album at a listening party in Paris. However, a release date and full tracklist had not been announced at the time of the report. The post Is Wizkid failing his fans in 2026? appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG disburses ₦39bn to tertiary institutions
item.description: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has disbursed the sum of ₦38.93 billion to 166 public tertiary institutions, nationwide, under the Needs Assessment Revitalisation Fund. Details of the disbursement contained in a statement by the Head, Media Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, Efe Ovuakporie in Abuja, yesterday, showed that beneficiaries included 79 universities, 46 polytechnics and 41 colleges of education. The funds would support approved projects aimed at addressing infrastructure gaps and improving teaching and learning facilities across the institutions. The university component accounts for ₦28.5 billion for 79 institutions, while 46 polytechnics have allocations totalling ₦5.8 billion. The 41 colleges of education received ₦4.7 billion. The statement read in part, “The intervention forms part of the Federal Government’s efforts to address the needs of public universities and support the implementation of agreed measures under the Memorandum of Understanding between the Federal Government and the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU). “The funds are expected to enable beneficiary institutions to commence or advance approved projects addressing critical infrastructure and other identified institutional needs, with the overall objective of strengthening the quality of tertiary education in Nigeria. The disbursement underscores the importance of effective coordination between the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Federal Ministry of Education and beneficiary institutions in ensuring that approved public funding translates into tangible improvements in educational infrastructure and institutional capacity.” The post FG disburses ₦39bn to tertiary institutions appeared first on Vanguard News .

He argued that the previous practice of printing money to sustain the economy was unsustainable, adding that the reforms would eventually yield benefits. On whether Tinubu had influenced former President Muhammadu Buhari to adopt better economic policies, Aburime said it was impossible to know whether the President had offered such advice behind the scenes, noting that influence did not guarantee acceptance. Kanu’s release will be resolved politically On the continued detention of Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Nnamdi Kanu, Aburime said the matter had assumed a political dimension and would ultimately require a political resolution. Soludo had previously visited Kanu in detention and pledged to work towards securing his release. Asked why the governor had yet to achieve that objective despite his closeness and relationship with Tinubu, Aburime declined to comment extensively but said efforts towards a resolution were not over. “The Nnamdi Kanu case has become a political case and it will be resolved politically,” he said. Monday sit-at-home defeated, Anambra back to life Soludo declared that the enforcement of the Monday sit-at-home order by armed groups had been defeated, with commercial and social activities returning to normal across Anambra. He said vehicles were moving freely and major centres, including Awka, Onitsha and Nnewi were bustling with activities. “The war has been conquered, and all the debris is buried,” he said, insisting that residents could now move around freely and that Anambra was back to life. item.title: Carrick unsure over Man Utd future after Bournemouth loss
item.description: Michael Carrick said he will do what is best for Manchester United after a 3-0 demolition by Bournemouth plunged his future as manager into doubt on Sunday. Winless in eight games in all competitions, the 20-time English champions slipped to within one point of the relegation zone after a damaging defeat at Old Trafford. “It’s a tough situation,” Carrick told Sky Sports. “What is next? I don’t know. “I’ll always do what’s best for this football club. I’ve said it all along, I don’t change that now. I love what I do. I love the responsibility, but we’ll have to wait and see.” Despite a dismal run of results, the United fans largely supported Carrick as he made his way off the field at full-time before they turned on the club’s players. “I have mixed emotions to have that connection with the supporters in the moment we’re in. I need time to digest that,” added Carrick. “I appreciate their support but the situation is where it’s at. We haven’t been good enough.” Carrick’s decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench and not even introduce the Portuguese international as a substitute backfired. Fernandes, last season’s Premier League player of the year, had criticised Carrick’s tactics after a 4-1 thrashing by Como on Wednesday. “There’s always times in games when you are trying to change the course of the game and to make a difference,” said Carrick as he swerved questions on Fernandes’s absence. “Those were the decisions we made today.” The post Carrick unsure over Man Utd future after Bournemouth loss appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebola: 53 Contacts, Including Healthcare Workers Under Surveillance, Says NCDC
